```{r, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
library(Rcatch22)
```

`Rcatch22` is an R package for the calculation of [22 CAnonical Time-series CHaracteristics](https://github.com/DynamicsAndNeuralSystems/catch22) (catch). The package is an efficient implementation that calculates time-series features coded in C.

## Core calculation function

The main function of the package is `catch22_all` which automates the computation of the 22 features. This can be run in a one-liner:

```{r, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
data <- rnorm(100)
outs <- catch22_all(data)
```

Taking a look at the returned dataframe, we can see a nice tidy data structure:

```{r, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
outs
```

### catch24

An option to include the mean and standard deviation as features in addition to `catch22` is available through setting the `catch24` argument to `TRUE`:

```{r, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
outs2 <- catch22_all(data, catch24 = TRUE)
outs2
```

## Feature list

A list of the time-series features included in `Rcatch22` can be viewed using the included `feature_list` vector:

```{r, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
Rcatch22::feature_list
```

Since version 1.0.0 (catch22 v1.0), every feature exactly reproduces a feature of [_hctsa_](https://github.com/benfulcher/hctsa) v3.0.0, so values differ from earlier versions for most features.
Several features were renamed to their _hctsa_ names; the old names still work as deprecated aliases.
`catch22_feature_table` lists each feature's name, short name, name before version 1.0.0 (`legacy_name`), and the _hctsa_ call that reproduces it (on `x_z`, the z-scored time series, or `x`, the raw time series):

```{r, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
catch22_feature_table(catch24 = TRUE)
```

## Short names and single features

Short names can be added to the output of `catch22_all`:

```{r, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
catch22_all(data, short_names = TRUE)
```

A single feature can be computed by its name or short name, giving the same value as `catch22_all`:

```{r, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
catch22_feature(data, "trev")
CO_trev_1_num(data)
```

## Features that cannot be estimated

Some features cannot be estimated for some time series (e.g., a constant or very short time series).
By default (`mask_nans = TRUE`), each such feature is set to a fixed value at the appropriate end of its range, so that `catch22_all` always returns real numbers.
The `masked` column (with `return_masked = TRUE`) shows which values were masked, and `mask_nans = FALSE` gives `NaN` for them instead:

```{r, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
constant <- rep(1, 100)
head(catch22_all(constant, return_masked = TRUE))
head(catch22_all(constant, mask_nans = FALSE))
```

A time series containing `NaN`, `NA` or `Inf` gives `NaN` for every feature (with a warning).
